codes.description: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 1)
codes.subsystem: Fuel and Air Metering and Auxiliary Emission Controls
causes: Exhaust leak near downstream O2 sensor
Upstream O2 or A/F sensor skewed
Low fuel pressure or restricted injectors
codes.notes: The downstream (post-catalyst) sensor trims the upstream fuel control. A lean post-catalyst trim often traces to an exhaust leak drawing air in near the downstream sensor, or to an upstream sensor that reads rich and drives the mixture lean. Review short- and long-term fuel trims and both sensor signals before replacing sensors.

codes.description: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich (Bank 1)
codes.subsystem: Fuel and Air Metering and Auxiliary Emission Controls
causes: Upstream O2 or A/F sensor skewed lean
Sensor contaminated by oil or coolant
codes.notes: Compare upstream and downstream sensor activity with fuel trims. An upstream sensor that reads lean causes the ECM to add fuel, which the downstream sensor then sees as rich. Look for real sources of richness (purge flow, injector leakage, fuel pressure) and sensor contamination before replacing sensors.

codes.description: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Lean (Bank 2)
codes.subsystem: Fuel and Air Metering and Auxiliary Emission Controls
causes: Exhaust leak near downstream O2 sensor
Upstream O2 or A/F sensor skewed
Low fuel pressure or restricted injectors
codes.notes: Bank 2 counterpart of P2096. Check for exhaust leaks near the bank 2 downstream sensor and compare bank-to-bank fuel trims; a condition affecting only one bank points toward that bank's sensors, exhaust, or intake leaks.

codes.description: Post Catalyst Fuel Trim System Too Rich (Bank 2)
codes.subsystem: Fuel and Air Metering and Auxiliary Emission Controls
causes: Upstream O2 or A/F sensor skewed lean
Sensor contaminated by oil or coolant
codes.notes: Bank 2 counterpart of P2097. Compare bank-to-bank fuel trims and sensor signals; a rich condition on both banks points toward a shared cause such as fuel pressure or purge flow.

codes.description: SCR NOx Catalyst Efficiency Below Threshold (Bank 1)
codes.subsystem: Fuel and Air Metering and Auxiliary Emission Controls
causes: DEF dosing injector clogged or crystallized
Upstream or downstream NOx sensor fault
DEF supply pressure or pump fault
codes.notes: Test DEF concentration with a refractometer and compare it with the OEM specification before other work. Perform the OEM dosing quantity test and compare upstream and downstream NOx readings during a steady drive. Dosing and sensor faults are more common than a failed SCR catalyst. Many systems apply an inducement (speed or power limit) if the fault persists.

codes.description: System Too Lean at Idle (Bank 1)
codes.subsystem: Fuel and Air Metering and Auxiliary Emission Controls
causes: Exhaust leak upstream of O2 sensor
codes.notes: Lean at idle that improves at higher RPM strongly suggests unmetered air, because a fixed leak is a larger share of total airflow at idle. Smoke-test the intake and PCV system, check brake booster connections, and confirm fuel pressure. Total fuel trim beyond roughly ±10% generally warrants investigation (general guideline — verify against OEM specification).

codes.description: System Too Rich at Idle (Bank 1)

codes.notes: Check for a purge valve stuck open (command it closed or pinch the purge line and watch fuel trims), leaking injectors (fuel pressure leak-down test), and fuel pressure regulator operation. Fuel-diluted oil can feed rich vapor through the PCV system at idle.

codes.description: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Lean (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.subsystem: Fuel and Air Metering and Auxiliary Emission Controls
causes: Aged or failed upstream O2/A/F sensor
codes.notes: Determine whether the sensor reports a real lean mixture or is biased. If the upstream sensor reads lean while fuel trims are strongly positive and the downstream sensor reads rich, suspect the upstream sensor or an exhaust leak at it; a real lean condition usually shows lean readings on both sensors. Propane enrichment or a snap-throttle test can check sensor response (general technique — wide-range A/F sensors report current or lambda rather than a switching voltage).

codes.description: O2 Sensor Signal Biased/Stuck Rich (Bank 1 Sensor 1)
codes.subsystem: Fuel and Air Metering and Auxiliary Emission Controls
codes.notes: A sensor biased rich makes the ECM remove fuel, so fuel trims go negative while the downstream sensor reads lean. Look for sources of real richness (EVAP purge stuck open, leaking injectors, high fuel pressure) and for contamination from coolant or oil consumption before replacing the sensor.
